witness_description: K = Q(√-3), O_K = Z[ω] with ω²+ω+1=0; p=3; wp=(1-ω); ε=ω.
refutation_explanation: N(ω)=1, so ω is a unit, and ω≠1. Since ω-1=-(1-ω) lies in wp, ω≡1 modulo wp. Multiplication by 1-ω has determinant 3, and 3=(1-ω)(2+ω), so wp has index 3 and is a prime ideal above 3. Thus this ε violates the claim.
search_space: All 25 Eisenstein integers ε=a+bω with integers -2≤a≤2 and -2≤b≤2, in fixed lexicographic order, tested for unit norm and congruence to 1 for the single pair p=3, wp=(1-ω) in Z[ω].
